inShort: A serves, and B returns deep and runs straight to the kitchen line, split-stepping on the way. A only blocks the third ball softly.
rules: B starts just behind the baseline, feet wide, paddle ready. A serves easy balls.
B split-steps on A's serve: a small hop that lands just as A hits.
B returns deep, into the back third of the court, to the middle or at A's backhand foot.
No pause: right after the return, B runs to the kitchen line.
B split-steps again just before A hits the third ball. A only blocks it back softly.
tooEasy: A serves hard and deep, and B still has to return deep and get both split-steps in. Even harder: B calls the target before the serve, "middle" or "backhand".
tooHard: B stays at the baseline after the return and works only on the first split-step and a deep return.
goodLooksLike: The return lands deep, B never stops after it, and both feet land just as A hits the third ball.
